properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/03/2024 to DAKOTA OIL & GAS CO in West Pike Run Township, Washington county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DAKOTA OIL & GAS CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/03/2024
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8189878
Permit API: 125-23051
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: West Pike Run Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/03/2024
Comments: On 06/03/2024, an incident inspection was conducted at the Zemba 1 well site following receipt of a spill report submitted by the operator on 05/31/2024 (CTS 381125). Penneco representatives on site. I called the operator on 06/03/2024 and they said that approximately 5 to 6 barrels were spilled on site and that the tank was cracked. The incident was discovered 05/31/2024 at 11:30 am and was reported to the Department on 05/31/2024 at 3:00 pm.Conductivity probe calibrated on 06/03/2024.The following was observed:The operator and well's information were posted on site, however the first three digits of the API were reading 126 instead of 125. I recommend that this is addressed. The tag on the well was displaying the last six digits of the API and not 125 (Photos 1, 2).Conductivity readings were taken at the site in the area that appeared to be impacted. A section of grass was dead and discolored near the tank (Photos 3-5). Readings were taken before and after calibration of the conductivity probe.Readings before calibration ranged from 25.4-852 uS/cm (Photos 6-9).Readings after calibration ranged from 227-1142 uS/cm (Photos 10-16).The tank was removed and additional readings were taken within the area with focus on the wet spots (Photos 17, 18). Readings were 20.5 uS/cm and 205 uS/cm (Photos 19, 20).The wellhead was in generally good condition with some corrosion (Photo 21).The Department requests the type of material released (brine or oil). The Department recommends that the Spill Policy is utilized due to a spill larger than 42 gallons. The Department also requests information on why the remediation was not started and/or the spill immediately addressed. Due to the observation of dead grass which is indicative of a fluid impact from the well site, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78.66(b), and 78.66(e) are being issued.

Violation ID: 966785
Permit API: 129-24375
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/26/2022
Comments: On August 26, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Janoscrat 1 well in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection CEI inspection in response to violations issued under inspection 3400883 where violations were issued due to a possible brine discharge that was discovered on July 29, 2022. The following was observed:The brine tank from where the possible discharge occurred in inspection 3400883 has since been removed, and the area has been mulched and seeded (see photos 1 and 2). The hissing sound and gas odor previously noted on the well head in inspections 3400883 and 3399998 is no longer present (see photo 4). Newly updated operator's information has also been added (see photo 3). Soil conductivity readings were taken on both sides of what once appeared to be the brine puddle. The one taken on the side closest to the well at the former location of the brine tank read, .49 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken on the side farthest away from the well read .44 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). An additional reading was taken on the side closest to the well at the former brine tank location, but approximately 6 inches of soil was dug before the reading was taken. It read .38 Micro Siemens. A background reading was taken 50 feet west of the well which read .24 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). Overall, the conductivity of the soil at the site of the possible brine release appears to now be comparable to the surrounding soil.Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of August 26, 2022. However, outstanding violations issued during inspection record 3400883 shall remain open since no NOV response or any of the information requested has been received from the operator.

Comments: Department received application for transfer of well permits for the Hickman Speerstra #5 well located in Venango County, Cranberry Township. Photo#1. Transfer has not yet been approved from PENNFIELD ENERGY, LLC. to LAKESHORE ENERGY DEVELOPMENT, LLC. Onsite to complete inspection before application approval. API 121-45712. Confirmed Coordinates. Well is equipped with rods, inside 2" tubing, inside 6-1/4" casing. Photos #2/#3. The casing and tubing are both open to the atmosphere. No venting detected at time of inspection. Photo #3. No pump jack is on well, and no production line is coming off the well. No label was attached to the well. No posting was observed on or near the location. On location was a vertical steel tank inside a plastic lined earthen dike. Photo #4. Also on location was a disabled track mounted service rig. Photo #5. No production records were found for 2023. Production reported to the Department for 2022 was 100 mcf gas for 120 days. No oil reported. No MIA records were found for 2023 or 2022. MIA reported to the Department for 2021 has 8 psi on primary production string with no corrosion. No fluid or gas leaks detected on site at the time of inspection. The condition of the well at the time of inspection shows it is inoperable and unable to produce. Well is considered abandoned. The operator is in violation of: OGA 3211(G) Well Permits-Posting OGA 3211(H) Well Permits-Labeling 78.88(E)-Mechanical Integrity of Operating Wells 78.121(A)-Well Production Reporting OGA 3220(A)- Abandoned Well. OGA 3216 (C)- Equipment not being used for production.

This well is abandoned as defined in section 3203 of the 2012 Oil & Gas Act.

Violation ID: 863865
Permit API: 117-20309
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-10-02
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a FUI inspection at the Tilden Marcellus LLC - Simonetti 801 located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 10/2/2019 @0845 hours. The weather was sunny 74 degrees. Onsite for the inspection was myself, Korey Starkey, DEP WQS; Jennifer Compton and Nathan Smelser, Tilden Marcellus; Farm Boy Excavation; Civil and Environmental Consultants, Inc. As of today's inspection, a large stain was observed on the gravel surface adjacent to the failed dump line measuring ~8'x4'(See Photo#1). Tilden's earthmoving contractor, Farm Boy, had used a small excavator to scrape the surface of the impacted pad area, fill slope (see photo #2) and dig a sump in the fill slope approximately 4' wide and 5' deep. Fluid that had accumulated in the bottom of the sump had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm(See Photo#3). Sample 4427-192 was collected from the fluid in the fill slope sump and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for SAC 942 analysis. CEC consultants had delineated the extent of the impacted area with white flags. The excavator, and CEC, were currently working to remove soil with an elevated conductivity in an area below the toe of the fill slope(See Photo#4,5). The excavated sump was then expanded across the fill slope. A wet gravel layer was observed ~3' below the pad surface that appeared to be the source of the >19.99mS/cm fluid entering the sump(See Photo#6). Jennifer Compton and CEC continued to screen the fill slope area and remove additional material. The impacted material was being staged on the pad surface, on the interior of the gas line, awaiting the delivery of more disposal boxes. Ms. Compton was also awaiting the delivery of a super sucker truck to remove additional pad material. Tilden Marcellus and CEC were advised to contact the DEP Environment Cleanups and Brownfields (ECB) Program to facilitate cleanup activities going forward. Violations cited previously in inspection report#2939891, dated 9/30/2019 are cited as OUTSTANDING against the 2H well, API#117-20309 at this time. We departed the site @1200 hours. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 345263

Additional screenings were conducted outside the delineated area and the readings were not elevated. A soil sample was collected (3442694) and was sent to the Departments lab in Harrisburg to be tested for SAC 530 plus, bromide, lithium, and strontium. Diversified is planning to go through the Act 2 for site remediation. Moody Environmental has been hired to assist them for site remediation. Violations have been cited.

Violation ID: 8277565
Permit API: 123-47222
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Loomis Lease tank battery. Elevated specific conductance in soils was observed beneath one of the stock tank's drain valves within the secondary containment area as well as throughout a swath of stressed and dead vegetation downslope of the Loomis Lease tank battery. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection.Evidence of a concentrated flow of fluids was observed just beyond the secondary containment diking. Bare soils outside of containment were observed to have been eroded in a manner consistent with the channelized flow of a large volume of fluid. The bottom of the eroded channel was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Areas downslope of the tank battery where the flow of fluid was observed to widen (visible via the wide swath of stressed and dead vegetation) were observed to have elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 5,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The downslope path of the released fluid was then captured by a lease road ditch approximately 150 feet downslope of the tank battery. Observations of elevated specific conductance in soils within the road ditch continued to a culvert nearby to the Loomis Lease Loomis 3 OG well. Standing water at the outflow of this culvert was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 1,300 micro Siemens per centimeter. Elevated soil conductivity readings in excess of 1,000 micro Siemens per centimeter continued for approximately 100 feet from the outfall of the culvert.The total observed path of stressed/dead vegetation and elevated conductivity readings was approximately 750 feet in length and up to 30 feet in width. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with receipts documenting the proper disposal of brine resulting from producing the Loomis Lease.

SPBUTs were initiated on 5/26/20 @ ~ 08:15 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in w/ Frac valves installed on top of well heads. Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 3/11/2024
Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8256579
Permit API: 083-46720
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/18/2025
Comments: I was informed by my supervisor that Bull Run Resources had reported a release at their Backwards L #3 well located in Hamilton Township, McKean County. A gathering line failed and an unknown amount of crude oil was released. The release traveled down a road ditch approximately 500 feet heading in a southwest direction to a culvert crossing. The release continued through the culvert heading north for close to 190 feet, before stopping in what is best described as an infiltration sump for the ditch line. The sump contained the release and prevented it from reaching Chappel Fork. JR from Bull Run was onsite with a mini excavator and a lined dumpster that was being filling with impacted soil. He is continuing to work his way down the ditch line removing impacted soil and debris. The sump will be cleared of leaves and debris before being pumped out. Impacted soil will be removed and disposed of at an approved facility. Future inspections will be performed to document the ongoing cleanup. Confirmatory sampling of the remediated area is expected to be conducted when remediation is complete. Documentation regarding the disposal of the contaminated soil is also expected to be provided to the Department.Please acknowledge receipt of this inspection and attached violations by emailing me at ebruce@pa.gov.

Comments: I conducted a follow up inspection of this conventional well that had a release occur in November of 2025, when a steel gathering line had ruptured resulting in crude oil contaminating ditches and soil. Initially the remediation of the site was progressing. There had been no signs of product at the under flow dams, there was no viable oil in the ditches. In preperation of obtaining confirmatory soil samples to evaluate if the remediation was sufficient, it was discovered another leak had developed on a different section of the same line. This operator indicated they will replace all of the steel line for this well with plastic/poly line. This release was caught early and as of now, appears to be less than 1 bbl of lost product and has impacted a minimal amount of soil.Bull Run employees had a roll off dumpster en-route to remove the impacted soil. The ruptured line was sucked out with a vac truck and will be removed while running new poly line. Further inspections will be conducted to document ongoing remedation efforts, as well as confirmatory sampling to show that the remediation is sufficient.

Comments: On 10/10/2023, I conducted an inspection due to an incident that occurred on 10/06/2023. A gathering line inside of the tank battery containment which is located 290 feet to the south from the Arnold #2, had failed and crude oil traveled down slope from the tank battery area, aprox. 90 feet away. A neighbor had complained to the pumper, reporting that they smelled gas on Wednesday October 5th or Thursday October 6th. The pumper had looked around and found nothing on those days. On the evening of Friday October 6th crude was discovered inside and outside the containment. Sam Harvey of Bull Run notified the Department of the release on the Arnold lease owned by Armac Resources on Saturday October 7th.The gathering line ran through the dike wall, it is not clear whether the dike wall failed or if the line leaked outside of containment or both. Crude oil is visible outside of containment. When I arrived on site, the area as seen in the photos was already mulched and seeded. I removed several patches of mulch and smelled the soil underneath he mulch, the soil had a strong distinct smell of crude oil. The southwest side of the dike wall has been excavated and the contaminated material was placed inside of a roll off that remains onsite. It is unclear how much if any soil has been removed in the downslope area below the tank battery.There is no evidence of production fluid in the road ditch located along Bauer Hill road. A boom has been placed in the dry ditch as a precaution. I spoke with Sam Harvey and Justin Hansen of Bull Run (who are contract pumping and facilitating the clean up for Armac Resources). I suggested that an underflow dam be placed at the bottom of the area that has been mulched (base of hill), this is to prevent any remaining production fluid from being washed down to the road side ditch of Bauer Hill which leads to an unnamed tributary of Glade Run.

Unconventional: Yes
County: McKean
Municipality: Sergeant Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-23
Comments: At 17:48 on Saturday (6/20/20), Doug Kepler reported a hose rupture on well pad D08-O that resulted in the discharge of 110-120 barrels of production fluid to containment. Doug Kepler reported about 8-10 barrels of fluid overflowed containment onto a gravel road. It was determined that the spill flowed for 3-4 minutes prior to being noted and then shut off. At the time of this inspection, the operator was in the process of removing the contaminated soil from the impacted area. The containment was vacuumed dry and then removed. A mini excavator and rolloff containers were brought on site. Screening was done of the impacted soil using a soil conductivity meter with a probe. It was determined that the production water flowed along the access road approximately 200-250 feet in a narrow band before exiting the road surface in a small depression. The operator had removed all the impacted soil in this stretch at the time of this inspection. They were loading their 11th container at this time. An excavation was developing deeper on the northeast side of the spill site, where elevated conductivity was noted several feet into the soil. The operator will continue to screen and remove soil today and for as long as necessary. Rolloff containers are being staged on the D08-O pad, which is just off the edge of the spill location. Further follow up of this spill location will be performed as necessary.

Comments: On May 14, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IRs 4179087, 4179852, 4179896, and 4179921.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/26/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 12/26/2026 in accordance with current regulations.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S Plan is present on site but has not been updated to depict streams and wetlands along the access road.- The entire length of the access road appears to have been graded, seeded, and mulched. - CFS remains improperly implemented or maintained at several points along the access road (Photos 3-8, 11-16, 19-21).- The outlet to Culvert 2 (Photo 12) and the inlet to Culvert 3 (Photo 13) remain blocked at this time.- Orange construction fence and CFS does not appear to have been installed along the access road where a wetland was identified by Department Biologists (Photo 22).- Sedimentation is observed at multiple points along the access road (Photos 6-7, 20-21).- Sedimentation at Culverts 5 and 8 appears to be threatening the stream, however no active discharge to the streams is observed at this time. - Regrading of the access road near the previous location of the production tank appears to have resulted in sediment being pushed to the end of the access road, which appears to be currently held by brush. No CFS is installed in this area. The Department recommends pulling the sediment back and installing CFS to prevent sedimentation off of the access road.- The well site appears to be seeded and mulched at this time.Violations remain outstanding for erosion and sedimentation off of the access road, failure to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, failure to identify wetlands and streams in the E and S plan, failure to maintain culverts on the access road, and failure to implement/maintain E and S BMPs.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8269640
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/01/2026
Comments: On 04/01/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County. The weather was 55 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last 24 hours. I arrived at 0930 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Ralph Babcock onsite. We traveled the area of the impact together. There are still two 24/7 water trucks onsite actively recovering fluids. Fluids above the release point were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~1080 us/cm (1 us/cm = 0.001 mS/cm) (photo #2). Those fluids continued traveling through the stormwater ditch into the active sumps (photo #3 and 4). They have excavated up to feet of material was removed from the ditch. The EC of fluids within the sump #1 and 2 was ~1.2 mS/cm. At that time Repsol instructed the truck operator to move his hoses below the sumps to start recovering those fluids which measured ~3.10 mS/cm (photo #5). The EC of the fluids that were directly entering the stormwater basin were ~540 us/cm. The stormwater basin has a containment in place (photo #7). Fluids were being recovered on top of and below the containment. ~60 barrels had been recovered today from the stormwater basin and sump #3. The EC of the fluids directly downgrade of the stormwater basin outlet and before sump #3 was ~5.1 mS/cm. The EC of fluids located below sump #3 was ~6.38 mS/cm. Brow/black vegetation was observed in that area (photo #11 and 12). We traveled downstream and the EC of the fluids were ~1.4 mS/cm. A spring intercepted the path of the flow from above grade. The EC of the fluids downstream of the spring was ~1.2-1.4 mS/cm. The EC of the marsh area was ~1.5 mS/cm. The EC of the UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the impacts was 25.3 us/cm (0.0253 mS/cm). Fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek at the upper confluence were field measured for EC at 2.4-2.7mS/cm (photo #18). From the upper confluence of the impact to the wetland inflow EC was 185.9- 225 us/cm (0.1859 -0.225 mS/cm) (photo #19). The EC of fluids from the UNT Rockwell Creek downstream impact was 379 us/cm.Repsol stated the stimulation activities for API #015-23994, 23995, 23996, 23997 and 23998 are scheduled to begin on 04/16/2026. Violations against API #015-23994 remain open at this time. I departed at 1100 hours.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to Eqt Prod Co in Center Twp, Greene County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-03-14 to Eqt Prod Co in Center Twp, Greene county. 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Eqt Prod Co
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-03-14
Violation Code: 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 844716
Permit API: 059-26084
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-03-14
Comments: On Tuesday March 12, 2019 I received notification of a produced water release, which was discovered and reported to the Department the preceding evening, at the Pierce Well Site located in Center Township, Greene County. On Tuesday, while on-site to assess the situation, I spoke on the telephone with Ms. Carey Valor Bell from EQT Production Company (EQT) regarding details of the incident and the remediation. I also conducted site visits on Wednesday March 13 and two (2) site visits on Thursday March 14 to check on the progress of remediation activities. Ms. Valor Bell was also present during the March 14 afternoon site visit. What was assumed to be an estimated two (2) to three (3) gallons of produced fluid was discovered at the Pierce Well Pad on March 11. The fluid was observed to be "bubbling up" through the well pad gravel along the northeastern side of the well pad behind the GPUs. Upon discovery, the GPU was shut-in to prevent any additional,flow through the dump line which runs between the GPU and the production fluid ASTs. Following further investigation, it was discovered that the initial estimated quantity was low given that the released fluid appeared to be seeping out of the slope immediately below and adjacent to the dump line. EQT currently estimates approximately 30 gallons of produced fluid had leaked from the dump line. A different remediation contractor was mobilized to the site to continue with the investigation and remediation. During the initial excavation of the well pad gravel, water was observed entering the excavation from the pad gravels which was assumed to be precipitation. Given that water was entering the excavation and the forecast for additional precipitation, a sump was installed in the excavation on the pad to dewater the area into a flow-back tank. The collected water will be monitored until conductivity readings meet applicable standards, at which time the well pad will be further investigated and remediated. While dewatering of the initial excavation continued, soil conductivity probes were used to delineate the extent of impact on the well pad slope below the GPU. The excavation limit was approximately in line with the outside edge of the GPU associated with well 591982 (059-26084) and extended approximately 10 to 12 feet west. The excavation was deepest (approximately 18 inches) along the eastern end of the excavation and was estimated to be approximately six (6) inches in depth along the western end of the excavation. A soil conductivity probe was also used to confirm that all impacted materials had been removed. Additional material was removed to assure remediation was complete. Conductivity readings collected following excavation activities were all less than or equal to 1 mS/cm. The impacted material was containerized and sampled for off-site disposal. The excavated area was stabilized with seed and mulch. Silt fence was also set up along the downslope side of the excavation. The sump was still running and connected to the flow-back tank as observed on a March 20, 2019 site visit. The release of produced fluid from the dump line and impact to native materials is a violation of 35 P.S. Section 6018.301 and 25 Pa. Code, Sections 78a.54 and 78a.57(a). The operator should respond according to the instructions provided in this notice.
